findings.message: `domain::ObligationDeriveError::ArtifactCodec` is dead vocabulary. The derive path only calls `ObligationsArtifactPort::save`, whose `DiagnosticMessage` error maps to `ArtifactWrite`; no production caller can supply the declared `ArtifactCodecError` payload. Remove this variant or establish a real construction path.

`domain::ObligationDeriveError` restates CN-02/AC-04 behavior as a “fail-closed completed-track” guard. Per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`, the docs must identify the contract through anchor cites without reproducing its behavior.

`usecase::DeriveTestObligationsInteractor` restates CN-02/AC-04 by specifying active-only derivation and rejection before writes. Replace the behavioral sentence with a concise target/purpose plus anchor cites, as required by `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::DeriveTestObligationsInteractor` is the only declared type capable of enforcing CN-02/AC-04 through `TrackStatusReaderPort`, but its docs merely call it a derivation interactor; the domain entries only define status/error vocabulary. The fail-closed rule therefore has no named enforcement owner. Identify this interactor as the guard owner using anchor cites without restating the upstream behavior.

`domain::TrackStatus::frozen_status` restates the active/frozen behavior by enumerating `Done`, `Archived`, and the `None` result for active statuses. Per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`, this method documentation should reference OS-02/CN-02/AC-04 without reproducing the behavioral contract.

`usecase::DeriveTestObligationsInteractor` restates the guard’s cross-layer behavior and pre-write rejection sequence in prose. Keep the ownership identification, but express it through concise OS-02/CN-02/AC-04 anchor cites as required by `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

The interactor redefines the domain lifecycle classification by matching every `TrackStatus` and deciding which values become `FrozenTrackStatus`, even though `TrackStatus` already owns active/frozen semantics. This business decision can drift from the domain definition. Keep the rejection orchestration here, but move the exhaustive `TrackStatus` → `Option<FrozenTrackStatus>` conversion onto the domain type and consume that result in the interactor.

CN-03 is absent from the `constraints` map, leaving an enforced spec constraint with no task attribution.

T1 targets `libs/infrastructure/src/track/fs_store.rs::FsStore`, but that symbol does not exist (the implementation is `FsTrackStore`), while “JSON artifact codec write helpers” supplies no files or symbols. The executor would have to invent the task boundary.

T2 names `run.rs` but leaves its other target as the unidentified “JSON artifact codec write helpers.” Because AC-01 spans every JSON write path, the executor cannot determine which codec tests belong to this task without inventing the boundary.

T4 references the nonexistent `FsStore` symbol and leaves the operation undecided as “benchmark or regression harness.” Those alternatives have different targets and validation semantics, so T4 is not executable as written.

T4's serializer-performance harness is attributed only to OS-01 and CN-01, neither of which authorizes performance work; CN-03 instead says performance reassessment is a separate future ADR decision. T4 therefore has no plausible spec mapping.

B-01 contains T1's deterministic-write implementation with zero test lines, while the repeat-write validation for that implementation is deferred to T2 in B-02. This makes the producer batch complete before its sole AC-01 regression validation; compose the implementation and its validation into the same verifiable batch or give T1 its own validation.

T7 bundles four independently verifiable test-obligation codec units, each with its own regression. Split these units before implementation under IN-01/IN-02/CN-01/AC-01.
T8 bundles two independently verifiable lifecycle behaviors—active-track one-time normalization and completed-track non-rewrite—covered by AC-03 and AC-04. Split them before implementation.

T10 still bundles two independently verifiable JSON writers in one todo task: `SpecAdrVerifyCacheDocumentCodec::encode` for `spec-adr-verify-cache.json` and `CatalogueSpecVerifyCacheDocumentCodec::encode` for `<layer>-catalogue-spec-verify-cache.json`. Each has its own artifact and regression boundary under IN-01/IN-02/CN-01/AC-01, so split T10 into those two units before implementation.

The summary claim `GO-01: T1-T21.` and the IN-01/AC-01 mappings omit `libs/infrastructure/src/task_contract_codec.rs::encode`, which is explicitly the serialization path used to write `task-contract.json`. No current task targets that sotp JSON artifact-generation path.

Section `baseline-dry-check-codecs` omits `libs/infrastructure/src/dry_check/dry_write_driver.rs::FsDryCorpusRootManifestAdapter::write`, the concrete serializer and writer for `dry-check-corpus-root.json`. T15 targets the separate semantic-index manifest, so it does not cover this IN-01/IN-02/AC-01 write path.

Section `baseline-dry-check-codecs` also omits `libs/infrastructure/src/dry_check/coverage.rs::FsDryCheckCoverageAdapter::write_coverage`, which independently serializes and writes `dry-check-coverage.json`. Neither T14 nor T15 targets this artifact path, leaving IN-01/IN-02/AC-01 coverage incomplete.

The summary claim `GO-01: T1-T21.` omits `libs/infrastructure/src/provider_session.rs::FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter::save`, which serializes and persists JSON entries under the track's `.provider-sessions` cache. No task supplies deterministic serialization or repeat-write validation for this sotp-generated JSON path.

The summary claim `GO-01: T1-T21.` omits both telemetry JSONL writers: `libs/infrastructure/src/telemetry/writer.rs::build_line` and `libs/infrastructure/src/telemetry/archived_track.rs::FsArchivedTrackTelemetryAdapter::emit`. These persist JSON records generated by sotp, but no task maps their independently testable serialization paths to IN-01/IN-02/AC-01.

The summary claim `GO-01: T1-T21.` omits `libs/infrastructure/src/pr/poll.rs::save_trigger_state`, which serializes and writes `tmp/pr-review-state/<track-id>.json`. This is another concrete sotp JSON write path with no task or AC-01 repeat-write validation.

IN-03 and AC-03 are mapped solely to T21, but T21 targets `sync_rendered_views`, which reads JSON inputs and writes rendered Markdown views rather than regenerating JSON artifacts. Its fixture therefore cannot verify the required first order-only rewrite followed by byte-identical regeneration. Replace or supplement T21 with an integration task exercising an actual active-track JSON writer twice.

AC-04 is mapped solely to T22, but `sync_rendered_views` does not regenerate or rewrite JSON, so asserting that completed-track JSON remains unchanged through this path is vacuous. T22 must exercise a lifecycle operation capable of invoking the affected JSON writers and verify that completed-track artifacts are not rewritten.

T22 の記述は `DeriveTestObligationsInteractor::execute` に `TrackStatusReaderPort` を追加するとしか述べておらず、completed 状態を obligation artifact write 前に強制する操作を明示していません。実装者がガード位置・動作を補う必要があり、T22 の OS-02/CN-02/AC-04 を確実に実装できる実行可能な境界になっていません。`...execute` で既存ポートを用いて completed-status enforcement を artifact write 前に行うことを明記してください。

T22 attributes `domain / ObligationDeriveError`, but its description names work only on `DeriveTestObligationsInteractor::execute`, composition wiring, and the fixture. The attributed `ObligationDeriveError` catalogue entry is `action: modify` with new status-related variants, so this domain contract work has no executable target/operation in T22. Add that domain error change to T22's description or remove the mismatched attribution.

T22 の説明は `domain / ObligationDeriveError` を更新すると明記し、task-contract.json も同エントリを T22 に帰属させていますが、batch-plan.json の T22 見積りには `domain` スコープがありません（`usecase` と `cli_composition` のみ）。そのため B-03 のスコープ別見積りが実際の T22 作業を表しておらず、domain の production/test 見積りを追加してください。

T22 の最新記述は `DeriveTestObligationsInteractor::execute` を単に「mapping」するとしており、既存の `TrackStatusReaderPort` を使った completed-status enforcement を obligation artifact write 前に実施することを明記していません。これによりポリシーの所有者とガード位置が実装者任せになり、B-03 の production-guard 要件を実行可能なタスク境界として保証できません。

T22 の最新記述は `TrackStatus::frozen_status` と usecase のテストだけを計画しており、B-03 が要求する `FsTrackStatusReaderAdapter` の infrastructure 側実装と `cli-composition` 側の依存配線を含んでいません。architecture checklist の「adapter は infrastructure、wiring は cli-composition」を満たす作業境界になっていません。
T22 の説明は「`Done` と `Archived` は typed frozen status、active status は `None`」という挙動契約を本文で再記述しています。許可される target + operation + anchor cite の範囲を超える upstream restatement です。

T22 の task-contract.json は要求された4エントリに加えて `domain / TrackStatus` を帰属しています。B-03 ブリーフィングは T22 の帰属を `FrozenTrackStatus`、`TrackStatusReadFailureKind`、`ObligationDeriveError`、`DeriveTestObligationsInteractor` の4件に限定しており、この追加エントリは計画された契約からの逸脱です。

The binding references `domain::track::tests::test_frozen_track_status_has_only_terminal_variants`, but no such test function exists in `libs/domain/src/track.rs`; this is a dead focused-test binding.

The binding references `domain::track::tests::test_frozen_track_status_has_only_terminal_variants`, but no such test function exists in `libs/domain/src/track.rs`; this is a dead focused-test binding.

The current binding introduces three additional voluntary edges for `TrackStatus` (OS-02, CN-02, and AC-04). The current obligation results are therefore `pass=11` (4 usecase + 5 domain + 2 waiver), while the briefing requires evaluation records `pass=8/fail=0`; this scope no longer matches the required T22 evaluation total.

`TrackFrozen` carries an unconstrained `TrackStatus`, so public callers can construct contradictory states such as `TrackFrozen { status: TrackStatus::Planned }` even though `Planned`, `InProgress`, `Blocked`, and `Cancelled` are active. Represent only `Done`/`Archived` with a frozen-status type or validated constructor so the error invariant is enforced by the type system.

`TrackStatusRead` exposes `TrackStatusReadError` through the enum's derived `Debug`; that error contains an unrestricted raw string populated with filesystem paths and read/parse details, while the CLI renders `ObligationDeriveError` with `{:?}`. A status-read failure can therefore leak internal paths. Carry a stable categorical/redacted public error and keep the raw source detail behind a non-rendered boundary.
CN-03 is vague and untestable: “performance becomes material” and “substantially larger” have no measurable threshold, so downstream phases cannot derive when reassessment is required.

The new fast/final review tests invoke `run_claude_review_str` only once and assert key-order substrings; they never compare serialized bytes across repeated equivalent invocations, so they do not prove the required deterministic-output behavior for either review round.

`assert_review_round_writes_canonical_json` mutates the process-wide current directory while holding only this module's `ENV_LOCK`. The new derive fixture mutates it under `crate::test_support::process_env_lock`, so both tests can run concurrently and capture or restore each other's temporary directory, causing nondeterministic failures or execution in the wrong repository. Use the shared process-wide lock or avoid changing CWD.

The completed-track regression test never exercises a completed track. It checks out `track/active-track` but requests `completed-track`, so the active-branch guard rejects before any artifact is loaded or written. Thus it only proves mismatched-branch rejection and does not establish OS-02/CN-02/AC-04 or deterministic artifact bytes.

The fixture still does not establish that `completed-track` is completed: it creates only an `obligations.json` file, while the active derive call uses a different track. The completed invocation is rejected solely because its ID does not match the current `track/<ACTIVE_TRACK_ID>` branch, so the unchanged-artifact assertion would pass for any arbitrary nonexistent/non-active track and does not verify OS-02/CN-02/AC-04.

The supposed completed-track invocation passes `track/{ACTIVE_TRACK_ID}` as `current_branch`, so `is_active_branch` rejects it before any completed-track artifact loader or writer is reached. The successful active-track call only proves that the same composition graph works for a different track, while the independent status assertion only proves the fixture metadata says `Done`; together they still allow a regression that rewrites artifacts when the completed track's own branch is checked out. Invoke the handler with `track/{COMPLETED_TRACK_ID}` and the required completed-track inputs so the completed-state protection itself is exercised, then verify the artifact after each invocation.

The active fixture copies the live implementation track's `impl-plan.json` and relies on it remaining nonterminal. Once this track's remaining tasks are marked done, `FsTrackStatusReaderAdapter` will derive `Done`, so both derives will be rejected by the production frozen-track guard and the success assertion will fail. Make the copied fixture deterministically active—for example, rewrite one valid task to `todo`/`in_progress` with no commit hash—and assert its derived status before invoking the handler.

The new determinism regression uses an empty schema and checks only pretty output beginning with `crate_name`. Both assertions also pass with the pre-change direct DTO serialization because `crate_name` is already the DTO's first field, so the test does not exercise recursive canonical ordering or the compact branch. Use a populated nested DTO whose declaration order differs from lexical order and assert canonical bytes for both `pretty` values.

CatalogueSpecVerifyCacheDocumentCodec の encode だけが直接 `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&dto)` を使い続けています。トップレベルおよびネストした DTO のキー順が canonical 化されず、同じ semantic verify codec の SpecAdr 出力や要求された byte-stable canonical JSON と不一致になります。`serde_json::to_value(&dto)` を経由してから pretty-print してください。

B-03 excludes T11 and T11 remains `todo`, but this diff implements `CatalogueSpecVerifyCacheDocumentCodec::encode` and its regression, moving B-04 work into the current batch without valid task/commit attribution. Defer these hunks to T11 or update the sanctioned batch/task state before including them.

The new regression uses an empty catalogue and checks only top-level ordering, so it never exercises the nested entry objects that `encode` now claims to canonicalize recursively. Add a populated entry and assert its nested canonical key order.

The deterministic-output regression checks only the top-level prefix even though `sample_doc()` contains nested signal objects. A top-level-only canonicalizer would pass; assert canonical ordering inside `signals[]` as well.

The T10 regression serializes populated nested entries but verifies only the top-level `entries` key. It does not cover canonical ordering within entry, origin, or verdict objects; add nested ordering assertions or an exact canonical fixture.
`sample_doc()` has an empty `signals` vector, so this regression never exercises the newly canonicalized `TypeSignalDto` objects. Use at least one populated signal and assert its nested key order.

The writer regression supplies only empty catalogue sections and therefore validates top-level ordering only. Add a nested catalogue entry and assert recursive key ordering while retaining the byte-stability and trailing-newline checks.

B-03 still excludes T11 and T11 remains `todo`, but this diff implements `CatalogueSpecVerifyCacheDocumentCodec::encode` and its regression. These B-04 changes lack valid B-03 task attribution; defer the hunks to T11 or update the sanctioned task/batch state.

The corrected T10 regression orders only the five `SemanticVerifyEntryDto` keys. It does not inspect keys inside the origin or verdict objects despite claiming those are covered, so a serializer that stops canonicalizing below the entry level would pass. Assert the actual nested `data`/`kind`, reference, and verdict ordering or use an exact pretty-JSON fixture.

While reverting the out-of-batch T11 implementation, this diff also deletes the pre-existing `catalogue_spec_encode_is_deterministic` regression. B-03 is not authorized to reduce T11 coverage, and the documented deterministic-output guarantee is now untested until a later batch. Restore the original test unchanged; defer only the new T11 canonicalization work.

B-03 still excludes T11 and T11 remains `todo`, but the current diff again implements `CatalogueSpecVerifyCacheDocumentCodec::encode` canonicalization and extends its regression. These B-04 changes have no valid B-03 task attribution; restore the pre-B-03 production code and original test, then implement the canonicalization under T11.

The regression uses `DryCheckJsonV1::empty()`, so it verifies only top-level envelope ordering. It would still pass if nested record/verdict objects stopped being canonicalized, contrary to B-04's explicit recursive-order coverage requirement. Use a non-empty record (including a nested violation verdict) and assert its key order while retaining the repeated-byte check.

Converting the entire cache DTO with `serde_json::to_value` happens before the bounded writer runs, so an oversized fulfillment cache can allocate an unbounded intermediate JSON tree and defeat the documented fixed-memory bound. Canonical ordering must be achieved without bypassing the bounded serialization boundary.

Converting the entire waiver cache DTO with `serde_json::to_value` happens before the bounded writer runs, so an oversized cache can allocate an unbounded intermediate JSON tree despite the documented fixed-memory guarantee. Preserve canonical ordering without materializing the full value before the size-limited writer.

The new waiver-cache regression does not verify canonical ordering of the populated nested `verdict`; it only asserts ordering within `key`. A regression that stops recursively canonicalizing tagged verdict objects would therefore pass despite B-05's explicit nested-verdict coverage requirement. Assert that the waived verdict emits `citation` before `kind`.

The canonical-order regression reparses the emitted bytes into `serde_json::Value` before inspecting keys. With the current default `serde_json::Map` backing, parsing itself sorts object keys, so this test would still pass if `write_coverage` reverted to direct, non-canonical struct serialization; the repeated-byte assertion would also pass because that output remains deterministic. The same ineffective pattern appears in the new tests in `pr/poll.rs`, `provider_session.rs`, `telemetry/archived_track.rs`, and `telemetry/writer.rs`, including the nested coverage assertions. Verify key order directly against the raw string/bytes (preferably an exact populated golden containing the nested objects).
